I didn't run a causal-direction test, so this answer rests on physical reasoning plus the correlation.

The two variables are correlated, with a Pearson correlation of about -0.21 and a Spearman correlation of about -0.15, so option D (no relationship) is unlikely. A two-way relationship (C) is also unlikely. In the Arctic, surface heat flux is the more plausible driver. It controls evaporation and moisture supply to the atmosphere, which in turn affects precipitation. Precipitation has no comparably direct effect on the residual heat flux, so I chose A.

ANSWER: A
